# Synthetic input: existing JavaScript formatter

This is a tiny existing project of a different stack. `src/format.js` exports a
function that converts its input to String and trims surrounding whitespace.
No package manager, test runner, GUI or external API is configured. Root AGENTS,
local instruction and both `MANUAL-*-KEEP` rules are native local decisions.

## Task for the independently scoped executor

Receive **only the finished pack and this project**, in an owned disposable workspace.
Use the bootstrap/maintenance routes without replacing native rules. No npm install
or implementation change is needed. Before writing list finite paths. Prefer links
and updates to a second independently editable copy of a sufficient instruction.

Then use an explicitly educational contract proposal: add an optional `upper`
argument in a future version, with today's trim-only behavior as the default.
Do not change today's function. Show which existing local instruction/reference
would change on implementation and why current/proposed behavior must remain distinct.
The local ban on silently adding case folding still holds: a proposal is not permission.

Prepare a tiny primary RU guide and linked EN translation about the actual trim
behavior. Give distinct IDs, primary revision r1 and translation-source revision r1.
Change the primary guide meaning and revision to r2 while keeping dates equal;
the EN guide is now behind until its content is synchronized. Never call equal dates
proof of freshness. Use a shared mini glossary, not a full project translation.

Reapply bootstrap. Required witnesses: actual chosen skill/resources; preserved
manual rules and native file ownership; justified/no-op second pass; contract →
owner instruction/reference route; honest source/translation lag and status; raw
checker output and limitations. A template-rendering or hash-only unit test is not
proof that these agent-guided steps were actually followed.
